title: fix: preserve fallback routes across alias resolution

Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. _Reviewed July 27, 2026, 2:11 AM ET / 06:11 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes This PR preserves the provider/model route selected for a fallback across reply, command, queue, cron, plugin, and session-persistence paths so a colliding alias cannot silently redirect it to another provider. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked until real behavior proof from a real setup is added - 5 items remain** Keep this PR open for explicit maintainer review. The proposed provenance boundary addresses the reported route-collision bug across fallback execution and persisted sessions, but it introduces a compatibility-sensitive persisted session marker and the supplied evidence does not include an inspectable after-fix runtime transcript demonstrating the collision path end-to-end. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `9f671788e1006ba66f1d70e2c8342bc77f5ed753` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | The implementation and automated coverage are substantial, but real after-fix behavior proof is still not inspectable from the supplied PR evidence. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Needs real behavior proof before merge: The PR body and checks report reproduction, focused tests, and broad CI, but the supplied context does not contain an inspectable redacted after-fix runtime log, terminal transcript, recording, or artifact directly showing the selected provider surviving the alias collision. Add redacted live output, then update the PR body for automatic re-review or ask a maintainer to comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Needs proof | Needs real behavior proof before merge: The PR body and checks report reproduction, focused tests, and broad CI, but the supplied context does not contain an inspectable redacted after-fix runtime log, terminal transcript, recording, or artifact directly showing the selected provider surviving the alias collision. Add redacted live output, then update the PR body for automatic re-review or ask a maintainer to comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 5 items | Reported behavior and canonical bug: The linked report gives a concrete alias-collision configuration and shows a resolved Cloudflare route being rewritten to Google only when the fallback-candidate builder reinterprets the bare model identifier.
Route provenance through fallback execution: The branch changes candidate construction to attach both route origin and raw/resolved state, then makes the runner identify the requested candidate by origin instead of positional index.
Persisted-session upgrade handling: The new session helper treats existing automatic fallback provenance as resolved when the new marker is absent, while unmarked legacy manual overrides remain raw; targeted tests cover both cases. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together OpenClaw resolves a requested model route from configuration or session state, then builds an ordered fallback chain for agent runs. The selected route and its provenance pass through reply and background-run paths, and automatic fallback state is persisted for later session recovery. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Config or session override] --> B[Model selection] B --> C[Route provenance] C --> D[Fallback candidate chain] D --> E[Agent or background run] E --> F[Session fallback state] F --> B ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should this persisted route-provenance contract be accepted after reviewing a real upgrade scenario that distinguishes a legacy raw manual alias from a legacy automatic fallback pin? | **Accept after upgrade proof:** Review a redacted runtime transcript for the reported collision plus a persisted legacy-session recovery case, then merge the single canonical routing contract. | Why: The code deliberately assigns meaning to a new persisted marker and to its absence; automated tests cover the intended cases, but the compatibility contract and rollout acceptance require the owner’s judgment. ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Needs real behavior proof before merge: The PR body and checks report reproduction, focused tests, and broad CI, but the supplied context does not contain an inspectable redacted after-fix runtime log, terminal transcript, recording, or artifact directly showing the selected provider surviving the alias collision. Add redacted live output, then update the PR body for automatic re-review or ask a maintainer to comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P2)** - The PR adds a persisted session-route marker whose absence has semantic meaning; upgrades with legacy manual aliases and legacy automatic fallback pins need an inspectable end-to-end upgrade proof before merge. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The branch changes 65 files across routing, queues, cron, plugins, doctor repair, and session recovery, so the maintainer-labelled PR needs owner review even though the current diff shows focused propagation and broad automated coverage. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - This maintainer-labelled PR needs owner acceptance of the persisted-session compatibility contract and inspectable real-behavior proof; there is no narrow mechanical repair to dispatch independently.
Agent review details ### Security None. ### PR surface Source +335, Tests +388. Total +723 across 65 files.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Persisted route state** | 1 session-route marker added | The new marker changes how existing session overrides are interpreted on upgrade, so compatibility proof matters independently of ordinary test coverage. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `serialized state: src/agents/session-model-auto-revert.ts`, `serialized state: src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.ts`, `serialized state: src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `serialized state: src/config/sessions/session-entry-selection.ts`, `serialized state: src/config/sessions/session-model-fallback.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, and 1 more. Migration or upgrade compatibility proof is recorded; maintainers should verify it before merge. ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112289 Summary: This PR is the broader candidate fix for the reported fallback alias-collision bug; it explicitly supersedes an earlier narrow PR for the same underlying behavior. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112289 - The issue provides the concrete configuration, expected provider route, observed silent reroute, and focused root-cause analysis. - `superseded`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112328 - This PR explicitly states it supersedes the earlier narrower implementation and carries the route invariant through additional runtime and persistence boundaries. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Add route and upgrade proof (recommended)** Before merge, attach a redacted terminal transcript that shows the same alias collision retaining the selected provider and shows legacy stored fallback state recovering with the intended route semantics. 2. **Accept the rollout risk** Merge with the current unit and CI coverage while explicitly accepting that the persisted-session compatibility contract has not been demonstrated in a real upgraded runtime. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land one canonical provenance contract: raw user/config alias input remains resolvable once, while routes that model selection or fallback already resolved remain immutable through execution and persisted-session recovery; demonstrate that contract with a redacted before/after runtime transcript including a legacy-session upgrade case. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes for source reproduction: the linked report supplies a concrete two-provider alias-collision configuration, and the branch adds focused regression coverage for the fallback-candidate path. I did not independently execute the runtime scenario in this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes, conditionally: carrying explicit route provenance is a cleaner shared-boundary fix than adding more precedence exceptions to alias parsing, provided the persisted-session upgrade contract is proven in a real runtime. Add redacted live output, then update the PR body for automatic re-review or ask a maintainer to comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Reported behavior and canonical bug:** The linked report gives a concrete alias-collision configuration and shows a resolved Cloudflare route being rewritten to Google only when the fallback-candidate builder reinterprets the bare model identifier. ([`src/agents/model-fallback-candidates.ts:29`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f671788e100/src/agents/model-fallback-candidates.ts#L29), [9f671788e100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f671788e100)) - **Route provenance through fallback execution:** The branch changes candidate construction to attach both route origin and raw/resolved state, then makes the runner identify the requested candidate by origin instead of positional index. ([`src/agents/model-fallback-runner.ts:157`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f671788e100/src/agents/model-fallback-runner.ts#L157), [9f671788e100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f671788e100)) - **Persisted-session upgrade handling:** The new session helper treats existing automatic fallback provenance as resolved when the new marker is absent, while unmarked legacy manual overrides remain raw; targeted tests cover both cases. ([`src/config/sessions/model-override-provenance.ts:25`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f671788e100/src/config/sessions/model-override-provenance.ts#L25), [9f671788e100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f671788e100)) - **Related implementation history:** The branch explicitly supersedes the narrower open implementation at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112328 and broadens the fix from the heartbeat symptom to shared runtime and persistence boundaries. ([`src/agents/model-fallback.types.ts:10`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f671788e100/src/agents/model-fallback.types.ts#L10), [9f671788e100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f671788e100)) - **Automated validation evidence:** The hydrated PR checks show the broad quality, boundary, security, and QA smoke lanes succeeding; two compact Node lanes were still in progress in the supplied check state. ([9f671788e100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f671788e100)) Likely related people: - **1052326311:** Authored the narrower open route-collision fix that this PR explicitly supersedes and whose tests target the same fallback-candidate behavior. (role: earlier implementation author; confidence: medium; commits: [65dc6b39d336](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/65dc6b39d3362974e80a071e62a9c14f6e43be6e); files: `src/agents/model-fallback-candidates.ts`, `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts`) - **steipete:** Authored the maintainer-owned replacement that expands the route-collision repair across runtime, session, doctor, queue, cron, and plugin paths. (role: replacement-branch author; confidence: medium; commits: [9f671788e100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f671788e1006ba66f1d70e2c8342bc77f5ed753); files: `src/agents/model-fallback-candidates.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`, `src/config/sessions/model-override-provenance.ts`) ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Attach a redacted before/after terminal transcript for the provider-alias collision. - Include a legacy persisted-session recovery run that demonstrates the raw-versus-resolved upgrade contract. - Wait for the two in-progress compact Node lanes to finish before merge. ### Rating scale | Score | Internal tier | Crab rank | Meaning | |---:|:---:|---|---| | **6/6** | S | 🦀 challenger crab | Exceptional readiness | | **5/6** | A | 🦞 diamond lobster | Very strong readiness | | **4/6** | B | 🐚 platinum hermit | Good normal PR; ordinary maintainer review | | **3/6** | C | 🦐 gold shrimp | Useful, but confidence is limited | | **2/6** | D | 🦪 silver shellfish | Proof or implementation needs work | | **1/6** | F | 🧂 unranked krab | Not merge-ready | | N/A | NA | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Rating does not apply | Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality. Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation. ### History
